mainText:
Election day is tomorrow, with the final poll putting Labour at thirty point seven percent, narrowly ahead of National on twenty six point four, and Opportunity on course to scrape into Parliament.

New Zealand.

The final The Post Freshwater Strategy poll has Labour on thirty point seven percent against National's twenty six point four, a lead of more than four points going into Saturday. Opportunity sits at five point one percent, just above the threshold needed to enter Parliament without an electorate seat. Opportunity's leader says he expects the party to get there. New Zealand First leader Winston Peters has called Shane Jones's description of Michael Laws's comments, reckless and foolish, after Laws's remarks about National candidate Katie Nimon. Christopher Luxon has repeated Laws will never be a minister in his government. Voting closes seven p.m. Saturday.

A survey has found Health New Zealand facilities averaged more than one priority one I.T. outage a day, with clinicians reporting disruption to patient care. The Health Minister has dismissed the timing as coincidence, days before the election. Separately, severe thunderstorms are possible across the upper North Island today, with rainfall up to forty millimetres an hour. Auckland Emergency Management warns of flash flooding and slips.

In Western Bay of Plenty, councillor Alan Kurtovich has confirmed his resignation was triggered by the council's Māori wards decision, forcing a byelection. Dallas Hohua, who stabbed a friend to death after a party, has had his manslaughter sentence reduced and may serve as little as two years.

Police say repeated copper theft has disrupted services, including cutting a school off from a student's medical records during a health emergency and leaving an eighty year old without phone connectivity for a month.

Hato Hone St John says it cannot fund specialist emergency response teams in Auckland, Tauranga and Christchurch, despite police backing for the units, raising the risk they will be cut.

World.

Russell Brand has been found guilty of rape and three counts of sexual assault at Southwark Crown Court. He has been told to expect a lengthy prison sentence, and police say they are investigating two further rape complaints. Sentencing is yet to be set.

Hoax bomb threats have struck European airlines and airports for the second time in a week, affecting at least twenty seven flights. The United Kingdom government has called it a malicious hoax, and investigators have not linked it to any state or group.

David Jones, Australia's oldest department store, has folded after one hundred and eighty eight years, with thirty eight stores continuing to trade under receivers while the business is reviewed. A breakdown in rent negotiations with its landlord has been reported as a factor.

More than two hundred and fifty thousand people joined strikes across France on Thursday over the cost of living, according to interior ministry estimates, with unions claiming the true number was far higher.

The Bank of England has raised interest rates to four percent, its first increase in more than three years, from three point seven five percent. Economists expect at most one further rise.

Technology.

Major tech stocks have fallen sharply, with the Nasdaq extending its slide amid fears of an artificial intelligence spending slowdown, as investors question whether near one trillion US dollars in A.I. investment is paying off. Intel shares continued falling. This follows Google's own five hundred billion dollar share fall reported yesterday over A.I. search cutting into its advertising revenue.

North Korea has denied involvement in the six point three billion US dollar Binance hack, which Binance says used fake job interviews to target an engineer. Users have withdrawn three point six billion US dollars from the exchange since the breach was disclosed.

Sport.

Formula One. Liam Lawson says he does not know what more he can do to secure his twenty twenty seven seat, despite scoring the bulk of Racing Bulls' points this season. His future remains unresolved.

Golf. LIV Golf has confirmed it will wind down after five years, entering liquidation after failing to secure enough player and investor backing for a planned relaunch.

Rugby. The All Blacks have made five changes to face Scotland at Murrayfield on Saturday, New Zealand time Sunday morning, with Jordie Barrett returning at centre. Fabian Holland and Scott Barrett continue as the first choice locks.

Rugby league. Kangaroos centre Kotoni Staggs has defended his decision not to sing the Australian anthem at the Rugby League World Cup, after criticism from teammates' stance drew public comment.

Football. The Wellington Phoenix face Auckland F.C. in their eighth derby of the season, nine months after a five nil loss prompted their coach to quit. Como beat Lens nine one in the Champions League, Anastasios Douvikas scoring a hat trick, the biggest away win in the competition's history. Real Madrid beat A.E.K. Athens, Federico Valverde scoring a late winner, to stay unbeaten in the group stage.

Coming up. Election day is Saturday the seventh of November, with voting closing at seven p.m. The All Blacks play Scotland at Murrayfield on Saturday, Sunday morning New Zealand time. The Wellington Phoenix face Auckland F.C. this weekend.

End of flash.
